artifact.notes: Demo model fitted on the synthetic demo book only (bre.demo.build_demo_book; 65 synthetic investors, 1040 sell responses). Every number it produces is a synthetic-training result. MAP via Adam (1500 steps, 3 restarts, best objective kept). Intervals: diagonal Laplace at the MAP over the population-level parameters; per-subject blocks fixed (200 draws). Calibrated context = at least 30 training sell rows.
training_data_refs: dataset:synthetic_demo_book (bre.demo.build_demo_book seed=0, 60 G_Q investors + 5 archetypes, 16 items each)
generator:bre.sim.gq POPULATION_DEFAULTS (synthetic default, not fitted to data); archetypes: bre.demo.ARCHETYPES (synthetic design choice (hand-written archetype), not a fitted value)

book_loss_response.definition: share of the book's clients whose predicted P(sell | L, no context, scenario-first) is non-decreasing over the five design loss levels [-0.05, -0.1, -0.15, -0.2, -0.3] (each client with its fitted random effects when known to the model, else at the population mean), and the mean predicted P(sell) per loss level across the book. A diagnostic of the served model's loss response, not a test of the data: the loss enters as a rotation of the state, so a non-monotone response is possible under the model.

capacity_definition: behavioral drawdown capacity: the largest loss L on the design grid [0.05, 0.1, 0.15, 0.2, 0.3] such that P(sell | L', ['news:recession', 'social:friend_sells'], scenario-first) <= 0.25 for every grid loss L' <= L, i.e. the last grid loss before P(sell) first crosses the target (0 when the smallest grid loss already crosses it). The loss enters the model as a rotation of the state, so P(sell | L) is not guaranteed to be monotone in L; the capacity therefore uses this first-crossing (prefix) rule, not the value at L alone.
generator: python -m bre.report (bre.report.generate_profiles): bre.predict.profile + predict_sell + Scorer.predict + drawdown_capacity; no fitting
